description: Grupo formado inicialmente por estudantes de Análise e Desenvolvimento de Sistemas do IFRO – Campus Ariquemes, unidos pelo interesse em tecnologia, inovação e desenvolvimento de soluções. Estamos sempre abertos a novos integrantes, ideias e diferentes áreas de conhecimento que possam contribuir para a equipe.
summary:
GeoTrend is an open-source, bilingual (EN/PT-BR) climate forensics platform turning 45 years of NASA POWER/MERRA-2 data (1981–2025) and NASA GIBS MODIS satellite imagery (2000–2025) into statistically verified trend dossiers for any coordinate on Earth.
Addressing "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!", GeoTrend resolves regular wet/dry seasonal cycles before running statistics. It filters -999 sentinels, stratifies observations into seasonal windows (Annual, Oct–Mar, Apr–Sep), and computes non-parametric Mann-Kendall significance tests, Theil-Sen slopes with 95% confidence intervals, lag-1 autocorrelation checks, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR multi-variable scans, paired with clear "correlation ≠ causation" guardrails.
Rather than mistaking single extreme weather years for climate shifts, farmers, educators, and policymakers get actionable proof. Our audited presets reveal Vilhena's dry season lost 234.46 mm of rainfall since 1981 (p = 0.000131), Ariquemes' minimum night temperatures rose +1.82 °C (p = 0.000001), Pantanal root-zone soil wetness dropped 5.60 percentage points (p = 0.000024), while Svalbard warmed +3.50 °C. Users export PNG Evidence Cards, CSV tables, academic citations, and permanent dossier links.
details: GeoTrend investigates temperature (T2M), minimum night temperature (T2M_MIN), bias-corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), and root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT) across any Earth coordinate via interactive maps, 20 curated cases, natural-language queries, or birth-date timelines (/explore). To defeat seasonal confounding, raw monthly NASA POWER series are grouped into homologous seasonal windows, then analyzed with two-sided Mann-Kendall tests, Theil-Sen slopes (95% CI), lag-1 autocorrelation flags, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control. Results render as trendlines, seasonal bars, Climate Stripes, and MODIS (2000–2025) Before-vs-After satellite imagery. Creative features include a Dark Editorial investigative aesthetic, offline-first resilience (bundled presets plus client fallback), PNG Evidence Cards with QR codes (9:16, 1:1, 16:9, academic figure), one-click ABNT/APA/BibTeX citations, CSV exports, and /dossier/:id permalinks. We prioritized regional Missão Amazônia utility (UN SDGs 6, 13, 15), bilingual accessibility (EN/PT-BR, °C/°F), ~50 km MERRA-2 scale limits, and Correlation ≠ Causation safeguards. Built on standard laptops using React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Leaflet, HTML5 Canvas, Hono, Cloudflare Workers, Cloudflare D1 SQLite, Open-Meteo Geocoding, Google Gemini API (with deterministic fallback), Biome, and Vitest automated test suites.
